_doc: Curated opportunist / concern list. Match is exact on species name. Drilldown badges fire only when one of these names appears in the top_taxa_up list (i.e., the species *increased* vs. baseline). Decreases of opportunists are not flagged. List is conservative; absence here means 'not on our list,' not 'safe.'

Staphylococcus aureus.note: Associated with skin and soft tissue infections; nasal carriage is a known risk factor for surgical-site infection.

Streptococcus mutans.note: Primary etiologic agent of dental caries.

Porphyromonas gingivalis.ref: Hajishengallis et al., Cell Host Microbe 2011

Tannerella forsythia.note: Periodontitis; member of the 'red complex' periodontopathogens.
Tannerella forsythia.ref: Socransky et al., J Clin Periodontol 1998

Aggregatibacter actinomycetemcomitans.ref: Henderson et al., Clin Microbiol Rev 2010

Fusobacterium nucleatum.note: Periodontal pathogen; emerging association with colorectal carcinoma.

Moraxella catarrhalis.note: Common cause of otitis media and sinusitis; respiratory-tract opportunist.

Streptococcus pneumoniae.note: Pneumonia, otitis media, meningitis; respiratory pathogen with carrier states.
Streptococcus pneumoniae.ref: Bogaert et al., Lancet Infect Dis 2004

Haemophilus influenzae.note: Respiratory and invasive disease; non-typeable strains common in adult colonization.

Pseudomonas aeruginosa.note: Opportunistic respiratory, wound, and bloodstream pathogen; frequent in immunocompromised hosts.

Klebsiella pneumoniae.note: Opportunistic respiratory and bloodstream pathogen; CRKP strains on WHO critical list.

Acinetobacter baumannii.note: Healthcare-associated infections; on WHO critical priority list.

Enterococcus faecalis.note: Frequent cause of UTI, endocarditis, and bacteremia in healthcare settings.
Enterococcus faecalis.ref: Kau et al., Cell Host Microbe 2008

Enterococcus faecium.note: Vancomycin-resistant strains are a major nosocomial concern.

Corynebacterium kroppenstedtii.note: Associated with granulomatous lobular mastitis and skin lipophilic dysbiosis.
Corynebacterium kroppenstedtii.ref: Riegel et al., Diagn Microbiol Infect Dis 2014

Corynebacterium jeikeium.note: Bacteremia and line infections, particularly in immunocompromised hosts.
Corynebacterium jeikeium.ref: Funke et al., Clin Microbiol Rev 1997

Candida albicans.note: Most common cause of mucosal and invasive candidiasis.
Candida albicans.ref: Pappas et al., Clin Infect Dis 2016

Malassezia furfur.note: Seborrheic dermatitis, pityriasis versicolor; bloodstream infection in lipid-fed neonates.
Malassezia furfur.ref: Gaitanis et al., Clin Microbiol Rev 2012

Trichophyton rubrum.note: Most common cause of athlete's foot (tinea pedis) and onychomycosis.
